sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
Fort Myers properties are valued by the Lee County Property Appraiser, and the Lee County Tax Collector sends the bill and takes payment. Those two county offices are the ones you deal with.

Property appraiser questions about value, exemptions and mailing address go to leepa.org or 239-533-6100. The tax collector answers payment questions at 239-533-6000. The tax collector's FAQ points out that levying authorities, listed on your bill, answer questions about ad valorem taxes and non-ad valorem assessments.

sections.h2: When are Fort Myers property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate taxes become payable on November 1 and are due in full by March 31 of the following year, according to the Lee County Tax Collector.

Paying in November earns the largest early-payment discount, which the state prints as 4 percent, falling to 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. A balance left unpaid as of April 1 falls under delinquent-tax law, and delinquent real estate taxes cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck.

sections.h2: How can I pay in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
Lee County's tax collector lists six ways to pay.

  • Online through its pay site, with a printable receipt.
  • Kiosks at any of six service centers, using card or e-check; e-check payments are free.
  • Drop-off at secure SmartLockers open around the clock at the downtown Fort Myers, South Fort Myers, Cape Coral and Lehigh Acres centers, while the Bonita Springs center takes drop-offs inside during business hours. Allow five business days.
  • By phone at 239-533-6000.
  • By mail, following the instructions on the bill.
  • In person at a service center.

The office says it processes payments within two business days of receipt, and the account history on its site shows PAID or UNPAID.

sections.h2: Can I pay in installments or over time in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
Yes, through the installment plan, the partial payment plan or homestead deferral, each with its own rules.

Lee County payment plans, from the Lee County Tax Collector
PlanKey terms
Installment planApply November 1 to April 30; taxes over $100 per notice; four payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three
Partial payment planCurrent-year taxes only; up to five payments per account between November 1 and March 31; no discounts; not available online or for delinquent taxes
Homestead deferralApply by March 31; age, income and lien limits; fire insurance naming the tax collector

The collector's page says an installment application for the 2027 tax year can be submitted between November 1, 2026 and April 30, 2027, and that if a property sells mid-plan, the new owner must continue the plan for that year.

sections.h2: Does Amendment 3 change my Fort Myers bill?
sections.html:
The Lee County Tax Collector says Amendment 3 does not touch the 2026 bill, which is due by March 31, 2027.

Its FAQ states the amendment takes effect January 1, 2027, and that any applicable changes would show up on next year's bills. For how the change affects your exemptions or assessment, ask the Lee County Property Appraiser.

sections.h2: How do the state limits affect a Fort Myers assessment?
sections.html:
On a homestead, Save Our Homes caps yearly growth at the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change; the Department of Revenue chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026 and 2.9 percent for 2025. Non-homestead assessments are limited to a 10 percent rise a year.

The Lee County Property Appraiser's home page offers video guides on the homestead exemption and portability, on the non-homestead assessment limitation and on estimating property taxes. They are worth a few minutes before you sell or buy, since a sale lifts the property to just value and the cap starts over.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption cover in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
The state describes an exemption of up to $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to every property tax, school taxes included, while the extra amount of up to $25,000 applies to assessed value above $50,000 and only to non-school taxes.

  • Apply on Form DR-501 with the county property appraiser by March 1.
  • The home must be your permanent residence by January 1.
  • The exemption ends if the unit is rented, stops being your permanent home, or you stop being a Florida resident.
  • Seniors, veterans and disabled owners may qualify for added relief, which the appraiser can explain.

sections.h2: What do I need to know when selling a house in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
The tax bill for the full year goes to the current owner of record, and the closing agent charges or credits each side for its share.

The tax collector explains that a change of ownership is recorded with the Clerk of Court and then sent to the appraiser, so a seller may still receive a bill because of timing. Forward it to the new owner or the closing agent. Mortgage companies that no longer hold a loan may still appear on the notice, so confirm there is no leftover escrow. After a sale, the next owner must apply for their own homestead exemption by March 1, and a sale resets assessed value to just value on the following January 1.

sections.h2: What if taxes go unpaid on a Fort Myers property?
sections.html:
Taxes unpaid on April 1 are delinquent, and by June 1 the tax collector sells certificates on them to the bidder who will accept the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps.

  • Certificate holders cannot demand payment from the owner until two years after April 1 of the issue year.
  • After that time, a holder may apply for a tax deed with a $75 application fee.
  • The clerk then holds a public auction, and the winning bidder must pay a deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater.

Selling before any of that happens keeps the payoff at closing simple.

sections.h2: Is there a rental angle for Fort Myers owners?
sections.html:
Yes. The Lee tax collector notes that tangible personal property used on a home's rental activity, such as furniture and appliances, can bring a separate tangible tax bill.

If you recently bought a home that is no longer rented, call the property appraiser's tangible office at 239-533-6140. Separately, renting out a homestead can end the exemption under state rules.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Fort Myers?
faqs.a: Pay the Lee County Tax Collector online, by phone at 239-533-6000, by mail, or at a service center. Six service centers have kiosks.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my exemption in Fort Myers?
faqs.a: Call the Lee County Property Appraiser at 239-533-6100. That office maintains exemptions, values and mailing addresses.

faqs.q: When does the installment plan application close?
faqs.a: It closes April 30 of the tax year, and applications for 2027 taxes open November 1, 2026. The first payment is due by June 30.

faqs.q: Why did I get a bill after selling?
faqs.a: Bills go to the owner of record when the tax roll is sent, and the sale may not have reached the appraiser yet. Forward it to the buyer or your closing agent.

faqs.q: Can I pay delinquent Fort Myers taxes by check?
faqs.a: Personal checks and eChecks are not accepted for delinquent real estate taxes. Ask the tax collector which forms of payment it takes.
